about: Writing for the slice. Plain data: every player-facing string of 'Raker's Morning' and Saltrow lives in these files and nowhere else. No code here.

rules.about: A dialogue card is one speaker turn in the lower third: at most three lines, each at most lineMax characters, already broken where they should break. At least half of Brea's turns carry a quantity or a bearing; those turns are marked "measure": true and the check (tools/gates/writing-w1.mjs) confirms each marked turn holds a number.

placeholders.about: Filled by the game at show time. Bearings are three digits, as on the compass strip.
placeholders.{bearing}: the live bearing from Brea to the thing named in the same line
placeholders.{key:NAME}: the key cap bound to that action (alidade, bearing, steady, interact, crouch, slot, pry)

worldFacts.about: Fixed numbers in the lines that the world must agree with. Each is from the bible; M1.6a checks them against the built slice and either the world or the line is corrected.

w2.about: Writing for the rest of the first hour: 'The Scar' and 'True Ground', Oro, the Holds barks, Field Books 5-10, the Ninewalls Guild Notices, the Transit's Sighting card and the cards that teach the herd, the wall, the re-survey and true ground. The same rules as W1 (rules above); checked by tools/gates/systems/writing-w2.mjs.
